fragments.text: So what is Reinforce Learning? Reinforce Learning actually comes from psychology where animals learn by trial and error, interaction in the world. In fact, so do people. And this is basically the idea that you do some things. You see what gives good payoffs, good consequences, and then you do those things more when you're in those situations again. And so the key aspect of this is that this is a type of learning that the agent for itself can tell when it's right or wrong. This is a different than classical supervised learning where people provide the labels. People say that's a cat, that's a dog, that's a hot dog. And Reinforce Learning, the agent, figures out on his own if what is doing is working

fragments.text: But luckily water treatment, especially in Drayton Valley, but generally speaking, is very, very simple. It's basically a two-stage process. You have water that comes in from a water source, in our case, the Norse's catch on river. It goes through a pre-treatment phase where basically you add some chemicals that cause solids to clump in the water. And the reason you do that is because the next stage filtration, we want to pull the clean water through and leave the solids there. And so if the solids are clumped together, it's easier to filter them up. So pre-treatment, filtration, and then into storage. Of course, there's a little bit of chlorine and chlorine added after the filtration stage, but that's basically it.
fragments.summary: But luckily water treatment, especially in Drayton Valley, but generally speaking, is very, very simple.
